title: Physical Quantities & Dimensions
notes: Physical Quantities & Dimensions. Any measurable quantity in physics is called a physical quantity. They are classified into fundamental and derived quantities.
Fundamental Quantities: Mass (kg), Length (m), Time (s), Electric Current (A), Temperature (K), Amount of Substance (mol), Luminous Intensity (cd).
Dimensional Analysis: Expressing a derived quantity in terms of base dimensions [M^a L^b T^c].
examples:
**Force Dimension**

Derive the dimensional formula for Force (F = m · a).

**Solution:** Mass = [M¹], Acceleration = [L¹ T⁻²]. Therefore [F] = [M¹ L¹ T⁻²].

keyPoints: Quantities can only be added or subtracted if they have identical dimensions.
summary: Basics of fundamental physical quantities, SI units, and dimensional formulas.
